name: Contagious
description: Enemy units [propagate] [effect0.power]. Add a copy of this card to your discard pile.
lore: The Angels once had an outpost where the roots of the Wild Woods met the sands of Limbo. That is, until the Fatal Elm decided it had had enough of their presence and released its spores.

name: Fetch
description: Add a random equipment with [ephemeral] to your hand and apply -[effect0.upgrade.costreduction][ember].

name: Soulsmelter
lore: A creation by the Pyreborne smelters and infused with a blessing by Fhyra, this staff consumed the souls of the bearer's enemies and transformed them into gold.

name: Cleave
description: Deal damage to enemy units equal to [attack] of the front friendly unit.
lore: “Although my brother taught me that strength is in dominion, the Banished proved that true might is in our unity.”

name: Windblade
lore: None can escape the Windblade's path, whose blade turns a breeze into a slice and a gust into a cut. For who can dodge the very air they breathe?

name: Frostpiercer
lore: “When my father's friends returned from the Void, so too did this spear appear along the banks of the Stygian Sea. And while the Guard rejoiced at the return of their sacred spear, I could not help but worry. Why would the sea return the spear now?”—Tales of the Inferno

name: Helical Crystalis
description: Deal {[effect0.power]} damage to the front enemy unit, twice.
lore: Physical combat has never been a strong suit of the Stygian Guard. Thankfully, their control of the energy coming from the Unnamed has made them deadly protectors of the inner Rings of Hell.

name: Purifying Cleanse
description: Restore [effect0.power] health and apply [burnout] [effect1.status0.power] to a friendly unit.
lore: Before entering a wax drip and applying new wax, a process I've been told is called “guttering”, Waxers are asked to cleanse themselves of any blemishes and impurities to keep the wax as clean as possible.

name: Spellweave
description: Draw a non-starter spell and apply -[effect0.upgrade.costreduction][ember].

name: Quenching Oil
lore: “I originally developed this oil in the Crucible to cool metals that water could not, intending to craft steel with a desired brittleness for a specific, delicate form of weapon. However, the resulting weakness proved too great for that use. While a failure for its initial purpose, the oil's property of leaving steel brittle has proven a wonderful weapon against enemies.”—Herzal, “My Workshop, My Life”

name: Pyre Light
description: Apply +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] to the Pyre. The Pyre then attacks immediately.
lore: The Pyre clearly has a mind of its own, as anyone who has been near it will tell you. Perhaps it's the latent mind of the former Titan it once was. Thankfully, it seems to still be on Hell's side.

name: Golden Touch
lore: “If you have to pay taxes, make sure you bury the tax demon.”—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #12

name: Gooey Flask
lore: The shroomfolk harvest the sap of the Fatal Elm when the leaves are at their most putrid. Once boiled, the sap becomes a tasty syrup that makes you want to curl up beneath a root and sleep.

name: Memento Mori
description: Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to [trait0.power]x the number of friendly unit deaths this battle.
lore: In memory, a Waxer is never truly dead. Through a process we developed together, their faces are embossed on deadly weapons and serve as a reminder of what once was and what will be.

name: Deadweight
lore: A chunk of the Pyre now devoid of any power. It just takes up space and is a bit of an eyesore. I've been unable to remove it from the train due to its enormous size and weight.

name: Furnace Tap
description: Apply [multistrike] [effect0.status0.power] and [emberdrain] [effect1.status0.power] to a friendly unit.
lore: Much to my dismay, the Umbra are able to withstand the heat output from the furnaces on the Boneshaker, allowing them to commune with its power and use it for themselves - at the cost of energy to the train.

name: Mushy Room
description: Apply [sap] [effect0.upgrade.roommodifier0.effect0.status0.power] to enemy units at the end of combat.
lore: “Do you think they'll make a wonderful perfume once the fungus is done with them?”—Madame Lionsmane

name: Penitent's Deathsuit
description: Can be equipped on enemy units.
lore: “No angel could survive this device. And I was the monster who created it. Perhaps I truly was more a demon now.”—Finna the Doomed

name: Preserve
description: Apply [freeze] to a card in your hand.
lore: Many precious artifacts of Hell were frozen when the Pyre was destroyed. Thankfully, this did not diminish their power, but only rendered their energy dormant until I am able to release them from their icy prison.

name: Blazing Bolts
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to a random enemy unit, twice. Add a stronger version of this card to your discard.
lore: Constructed bolts I gifted to the Umbra to dig deeper into the stone. When Morsels cannot break through it, these white-hot steel bolts should get the job done.

name: Wicklash
description: Apply +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] and [burnout] [effect1.status0.power] to a friendly unit.
lore: Those who truly cannot wait for their wax to melt can fasten additional wicks to their bodies, ensuring they burn with a brief, but beautiful, light.

name: Railforged Spike
lore: “When Heph and I drove the Spike into the very heart of the Rail, the steel sung with a deep, thunderous crescendo. With this singular, profound act, my daughter, the Stewards, and I were no longer a collection of machines and blacksmiths, we were the Railforged.”—Herzal, “My Workshop, My Life”

name: Forgone Power
description: Apply [frostbite] [effect0.status0.power] to the front enemy unit.[halfbreak]Discard a card at random.
lore: The Martyr speaks of the power a name has over the soul, that the Titan released its name for the good of Heaven, Hell, and Humans. Perhaps the same practice observed by the Stygian Guard is an evolution of this and grants them some minimal power as well.

name: Dragon's Breath
description: Apply [pyregel] [effect0.status0.power] and deal [effect1.power] damage to enemy units.
lore: As Keeper of Hell's Heart, Fhyra was a tenacious guardian. Those who tried to enter the caves beneath the last circle and steal her treasure would meet a fire hotter than Heaven's might.

name: Imprisoned Zephyr
lore: “Before they were corrupted, many angels were sent to the dungeons of Heaven to test their loyalty to Seraph. Many did not survive.”

name: Revenge of the Damned
lore: The quiet of a cairn grinds away even the strongest of souls. I'd thought this silence a testament to their unusual obedience, and, in a way, I was correct. Once I saw the pit of damned kinstones, I knew this clan was the same as all others — no stranger to disagreements or strict punishment. Once, long ago, I would've admired such Judgement. But what place do I have to think of that now.

name: Reanimation Lab
description: Friendly units gain +[effect0.upgrade.charactertrigger0.effect0.upgrade0.bonusdamage][attack] and +[effect0.upgrade.charactertrigger0.effect0.upgrade0.bonushp][health] on [summon] and [reanimated].
lore: The deepest and most secretive part of Orechi's lab. Only a few of his most trusted assistants are allowed inside and seem happy for the privilege. His other employees pray they never go there.

name: A Fatal Melting
description: Deal damage to enemy units equal to [trait0.power]x the number of friendly unit deaths this battle.
lore: Charged with both the extension of life and the acceleration of melting, the Reformed tend to large flames at each Votive House, allowing for Waxers to congregate and melt more quickly than they would on their own.

name: Discordant Toll
lore: As Dominion arrived upon Heaven its acolytes began to ring the bells, their hands bloodied until they could ring no more.

name: Infectory
lore: “Thanks for the ride!” cried the funguy as they leapt from the demon's torso. The angel gurgled in horror.

name: Fenix Fire
description: Deal damage equal to this unit's attack. Apply [pyregel] [effect1.status0.power] to enemy units.

name: Eager Conscript
lore: You never fight just one shroomfolk. Beneath Hell's topsoil is an army that can decay the mightiest of oaks.

name: Resin Blades
description: Return to hand when equipped unit is destroyed.
lore: It is because of blades such as these that the Reformed lament the process of molding the remains of their brethren into new weapons. They understand that each time the steel reforms itself, the trapped soul within the wax is struggling to be free.

name: Hexscalation
lore: “Draw the runes on the ground and wait for your enemy to arrive. They will be welcomed by a nasty surprise.”—The Ritual Tome

name: Weapons Cache
description: When you summon a friendly unit, draw an Equipment and apply -[effect0.upgrade.charactertrigger0.effect0.upgrade.costreduction][ember].
lore: “Although I do not know who forged these weapons, I do know the Skull Crusher's armory always seemed to know when I needed them most.” —Tales of the Inferno

name: Dominion's Eye
description: Non-Scourge and non-Blight cards in hand cost +[trait0.power][ember].
lore: When I first saw Dominion's effect on my fellow angels, I thought I had fallen into a nightmare. For their bodies were no longer their own, torn apart and reassembled by monster limbs.

name: Heroic Dive
description: [descend] then [advance] a friendly unit. Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to [effect2.power_unmodified]x this unit's [health] and [armor].
lore: “I flew past arrows until I found Talos defending the southern gate. The sight of her wounds pushed me forward. I called upon my strength. I was almost there, she only had to hold on!”

name: Kindle
lore: The Umbra Shroud mines the depths of the Crucible, creating more vents to the surface above. These allow the ember below to burn ever more fiercely, and when applied to the Boneshaker, the same technique has allowed us to increase our fuel efficiency for short amounts of time.

name: Armament Drive
description: Add a +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] +[effect0.upgrade.bonushp][health] Crafted Equipment to your hand for each unequipped friendly unit.
lore: “Heh, you want somethin' to kill angel zombies? Have I got the blade for ya.”—Heph

name: Witchweave
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to an enemy unit or restore [effect1.power] health to a friendly unit.
lore: As the fighting continued outside the temple walls, Lady Ekka prepared her strike. “May the moon's light and darkness unite,” she whispered.

name: Spike of the Banished
lore: “Talos asked me if I was certain. Once the Spike was in the Rail, we would forever be tied to the clans of Hell. I nodded. This is what Herzal would have wanted.”—Tome of the Lost Path

name: Crucible Extension
lore: The number of Morsels within the Crucible seems to be endless, making the work they accomplish proceed near instantaneously. Should I need to do future work on the Boneshaker, I will remember to take this into account.

name: Moonlit Glaive
lore: At the end of the Plenilune, the priestess return all weapons to the Silent. For now that the blades have been blessed by the Empress Moon, they have no place in her temple.

name: Duality
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to an enemy unit or restore [effect1.power] health to a friendly unit.
lore: “Silent or Selene, magic user or fighter, we are each a part the whole.”—The Ritual Tome

name: Emerge
description: Remove [stasis]. Starts battle on cooldown. Removes ability on use.

name: Weaponcraft II
description: Add a +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] and +[effect0.upgrade.bonushp][health] Crafted Equipment to your hand.

name: Moonrise
lore: “I wove the cloth across my wrists and waited for the moon to rise. As I saw it peak over the horizon, my powers grew.” —The Ritual Tome

name: Overdrive
description: Spend your remaining [ember]. Gain [burst] [trait0.power] for each ember spent.

name: Resonant Ruin
lore: Do you not hear the sound? It tolls for you, and the sweet embrace of madness.

name: Offering Token
lore: Making offerings to the Unnamed Titan has become a religious experience among the Stygian Guard. These offerings are made with such frequency that I helped to create tokens to represent a Guard's offering to the Titan and simplify the process.

name: Lava Flow
lore: When Hell froze, so did the mighty lava river beneath the Pyreborne caves. Once the Pyreborne melted the celestial ice, they restored the river to its ancient might.

name: Wildwood Sap
lore: When sap from Wildwood trees is consumed, it imparts the healing power of their reproductive spores. I also quite enjoy its floral sweetness.

name: Wurmkin Etchings
description: Return [effect0.power] consumed spells to the top of your draw pile.
lore: Even without sight or voice the Wurmkin have created a wealth of knowledge unlike anything ever seen in this Realm. Their approach to written language is ingenious, embracing knowledge and never letting it fade. By carving into the stone itself, stoneform as I've named it, the Wurmkin can record knowledge for nigh eternity. And even when the etchings of the stone eventually fade, the Echoes will continue to glow with the knowledge they contain.

name: Benevolence
description: Restore friendly units to full health and grant +[effect1.upgrade.bonushp][health].

name: Hosting Kin
lore: There is no mistaking the lineage connecting the Wurmkin to the Bogwurm Titan, but the hard-shelled Kinhosts do strike me as odd residents of this place. Some discarded stoneform mentions that they were the original inhabitants of this Ring, once a verdant place, but were enslaved by the Wurmkin as Echo vessels. Stoneform claims this was a blessing to the previously languishing Kinhost, an elevation of their lowly status. However, these discarded records and dismissive rationales make me think them to be downplayed atrocities.

name: Mortal Entrapment
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage and apply [dazed] [effect1.status0.power] to an already damaged unit.
lore: While molds are used in the resurrection of Waxen, the invasion of Hell has forced the Waxen to repurpose these molds for a more deadly effect. They are now positioned to trap unsuspecting targets who've already been injured, making them easier to encase in the hot wax.

name: Blazing Bolts
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to a random enemy unit, four times.
lore: Constructed bolts I gifted to the Umbra to dig deeper into the stone. When Morsels cannot break through it, these white-hot steel bolts should get the job done.

name: Gem Trove
description: Apply [damageshield] [effect0.status0.power] to friendly units. Add [effect1.secondarypower] uncommon or rare [snack] units to your hand.
lore: It is said that the Crucible was formed when the Pyre first ignited, molding and melting the nearby ground to create endless, winding caverns. The Umbra have done their best to direct me through these tunnels, but the maze of caves has still been enough to trap me for days at a time.

name: Plink
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to a random enemy unit, twice.
lore: The Primordium does not speak through words but through floods of feeling. The bounds of its mind seem endless. It's no wonder that the ultimate split of the Primordium created a varying number of personalities, not the least of which are my friendly Morsels.

name: Mine Collapse
lore: While Morsels seem to be quick workers in their mine, they do not appear to be the most intelligent and have been the cause of many easily avoided accidents. I can only hope this will not be the case aboard the train.

name: Spike of the Legion
lore: Whenever anyone has tried to build the Rail through the Underlegion's realm, they found the iron overcome by spores and fungi.

name: Echo Infusion
lore: I've only just arrived and, yet, I feel as though I've spent a lifetime here. When I sleep, I dream of Titans I've never met and Divinities creating worlds on a whim. I did not know of Exiles until they revealed themselves to me, yet now I see the very crystals that made up their Shardsouls. Am I losing my mind, or worse… am I finding it again?

name: Battering Ram
description: Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to [trait0.power]x [armor] on friendly units.
lore: Working with the Railbeaters, I was able to devise a series of interlocking shields that turn the Hellhorned into a mobile battering ram.

name: Restore
lore: One of the many strengths of the Channelers of the Wildwood is their ability to heal their fellow Awoken. Upon our completion of the Rail, they agreed to extend this practice to other Hellborne in need.

name: Bounding Echoes
lore: I'd done my best to abandon guilt and grief all those years ago, but now that their spectre returns, so do the memories of why we met in the first place. To cope, the Wurmkin have given me a place in their cairns — a study of sorts — to tinker away on these crystals. It helps, but not much. For each new discovery I find, another memory terrorizes my dreams.

name: Begone
description: [retreat] the front enemy unit. Apply [meleeweakness] [effect1.status0.power] to enemy units.
lore: “Will you stop your preaching?!” cried Fel. With a single flutter of her wings, she sent a dozen angels tumbling to the ground.

name: Moonbeam
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to the front enemy unit [x] times.
lore: “As our beloved moon fell, our home had one last gift to give our coven. When it shattered, all the magic we had stored inside struck Seraph.”—Ardania, fallen guard to Lady Ekka

name: Ice Tornado
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to a random enemy unit, three times.
lore: The brutal ecosystem of the Stygian Sea has evolved into a favorable place for tornadoes to destroy anything standing above the surface of the water. Thankfully for the Guard, their gills allow them to take refuge beneath the waves.

name: Ember Cache
description: Add [effect0.secondarypower] Excavated Ember cards to your discard pile.
lore: I created fortified steel boxes to house the dormant Ember mined in the Crucible, increasing its effectiveness through pressure and time.

name: Unnamed Tome
lore: When the Titan was finally put to rest, the Stygian Guard was formed. Tethys and I wrote this tome to record the existence of the Unnamed Titan and prophesize its return.

name: Forever Consumed
description: Deal [trait0.power][x] damage to the front enemy unit.
lore: Of a collective mind, the massive Umbra Shroud can wreak devastating damage upon the unfortunate soul who has been targeted by its wrath. On the one occasion I was witness to such an event, I was unable to return to the Crucible for months, afraid of the slightest chance it could happen to me.

name: Perfect Insanity
lore: Another memory: at the time of the Exodus, we thought that these Exiles, these souls to be sacrificed, would bring back peace, or some semblance of it. Instead, the Child was fractured and the souls of Heaven and Hell made immortal. Some of the Child's power remains in Heaven's Light and in the Pyre, but how can those small divine remains make up for millennia of suffering?

name: Pyrespeak II
description: Add a 0[ember] Pyreshot to your hand with [consume].

name: Wyngh's Radiance
lore: With an aching heart, Lieutenant Talos lifted her old friend's spear and prayed to Wyngh for protection. She felt a familiar warmth fill her heart. Perhaps it was her friend, not Wyngh, who answered.

name: Proliferate
lore: Within moments, the shroomfolk had devoured the demon's hand and began consuming their way toward his head.

name: Challenge
lore: “The new recruit stood on the bodies of her fallen enemies and pointed towards the Walls. Although she spoke no words, the challenge to Heaven was clear.”—Tome of the Lost Path

name: Steel Pulley Claw
lore: “The pulley needed a little dusting off when I found it but it worked like a charm. You should have seen dad's face when he saw it inside the Skullcrusher.”—Heph

name: Restoration Detonation
description: Restore [effect0.power] health to a friendly unit. Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to [effect0.secondarypower]x the amount healed.
lore: Though usually avoided because of its potentially deadly outcome, an Awoken's ability to impale themselves with thorns allows them to become a walking nest of spores. Upon bursting, the spores provide additional life with the extra benefit of damage to those nearby.

name: Tome of Horrors
lore: “My assistant gifted me this journal so I could take meticulous notes of my experiments. He might have also said ‘writing would help process my feelings.' I didn't pay much attention.”—Dr. Orechi

name: Siren's Song
description: At the start of the combat, [ascend] non-boss enemy units on this floor and apply [dazed] [effect0.upgrade.roommodifier0.effect0.status0.power].
lore: I've heard no song as beautiful or as deadly as that of the Sirens of the Stygian. Their luring voices can disarm even the most hardened of hearts.

name: Engulfed in Smoke
lore: In the dangerous depths of Hell, it's important to have the means for quick concealment. If needed, I've found that wicks bundled together will burn slowly and create large quantities of smoke.

name: Foundry Line
description: Choose a card. [smelt] all cards in hand, except the chosen card.
lore: The foundry took whatever scrap the forges could melt and route it into new molds. Little regard was given to what entered the melt, only to what could be made from it.

name: Cave In
lore: I've only seen the aftermath, but when a level of the Crucible collapses, very few Morsels survive. The Umbra don't even care to check for survivors, choosing instead to spawn new Morsels.

name: Frozen Lance
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to the front enemy unit.
lore: An ancient relic of a time before the Covenant. When I first came to the Stygian Sea, every resident of the Ring carried one to aid in their defense of the reigning Titan. There still lies some magic within the surrounding ice.

name: Stoic Platemail
lore: A suit of armor tailor-made for warriors whose bark is louder than their bite.

name: Time Stop
description: Apply [freeze] to all cards in hand.

name: The Reaping
description: Apply [corruptpoison] [effect0.status0.power] to enemy units on all floors.

name: Stasis Crystal
lore: “I am happy the Exiles escaped and all, but...how? Have the Shardsouls been weakened by the corruption? If so, who knows what else might escape...”—Tales of the Inferno

name: Glittering Draught
lore: “Once done, this draught will transform sunlight into moonlight and heal a fae of any wound.”—The Ritual Tome

name: Fenix Fire II
description: Deal damage equal to this unit's attack. Apply [pyregel] [effect1.status0.power] to enemy units.

name: Tiresome Climb
lore: Alongside the few remaining Hellhorned scholars, I designed the Boneshaker to change its shape at will, creating hallways that stretch to near infinity for the Winged who choose to walk them.

name: Pyre Plating
lore: “All my waking hours were devoted to finding a method to constrain the Pyre Heart. If I found no solution, the train would not be able to run, and without the train, peace was irrelevant because it could not be achieved.”—Herzal, “My Workshop, My Life”

name: Silver Ink
description: Apply [attuned] and +[effect1.upgrade.bonusdamage] [magicpower] to spells in your hand.
lore: “Take stardust and mix it with oil. Cast a blessing. Only the fae shall read your words written in this ink.”—The Ritual Tome

name: Grow Room
description: All units [propagate] [effect0.upgrade.roommodifier0.effect0.power] at the end of combat.
lore: “Do you think they'll be angry that we're in here?” whispered a small crimini. “If they are,” began his brother, “We'll take care of them.”

name: Engraft
lore: When in a dangerous situation, the Awoken sometimes cannot afford the time it takes to regrow limbs. While less effective, they will splice together severed appendages in favor of speed, but in my experience the binding does not last long.

name: Cycle of Life
lore: When a soul is trapped by vines, the Wildwood gives it new life. And when the soul is released after the vines wilt away, that life is returned to the Wildwood and the others trapped within it.

name: Wind-Up Punch
description: Attack immediately. Remove all stacks of [burst].

name: Resurgence II
description: Remove [stasis] and gain +[effect1.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] and +[effect1.upgrade.bonushp][health] per [stygianblessing]. Removes ability on use.

name: Faulty Body
description: Apply [fragile] and [spikes] [effect1.status0.power] to a friendly unit.
lore: “Poor Baron, he found a way to strengthen his love's frail body but, just as beryllium is strong yet fragile, so too became Inga.”—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Freeze Ray
description: Apply [freeze] to a card in hand.

name: Devilish Details
lore: “Nothing is off the market, not even the Pyre itself.”

name: Silver Strike
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to the front enemy unit.
lore: “Our defeat was certain but Lady Ekka urged us to continue until the full moon. Then, she explained, she might be able to alter our fates.”—Ardania the Forbidden

name: Titan's Gratitude
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to the front enemy unit.[halfbreak]Discard a card at random.
lore: From what Tethys has told me, the Unnamed below is not dead, but it is also not quite alive. The Stygian take responsibility for its well-being by providing sustenance, in return for occasional protection in the form of expelled energy.

name: Spiky Skin
lore: “I took a sample from a demon's flesh whose skin was as strong as steel and combined it with a bristle brush. Voila! My sharpest creation!”—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Hammerfall
description: Deal [trait0.power][x] damage to an enemy unit or apply +[trait1.power][x][attack] to a friendly unit.
lore: “Some hammers are meant to forge weapons and armor, while others were meant to bend steel thick enough to hold a rail together.”—Herzal, “My Workshop, My Life”

name: Celestial Storm
lore: “Lady Ekka fell silent as she called upon her ancient ally: the sky. Seraph's army had underestimated her might.”—Ardania the Forbidden

name: Zone of Silence
lore: A space made for silent meditation.

name: Dig Deep
description: [spawn] [effect0.power]. For every [trait0.tertiarypower] cards in your deck [spawn] [trait0.power] more.
lore: “Come sit with us in the shade. Don't worry, we won't hurt you.”

name: Tidal Turning
description: Restore [effect0.power] health to friendly units. Healing over max health applies [armor] instead.
lore: Moonlit shores attract millions of tiny fae to bathe in the moonlight. As the night deepens, the Selene dance, guided by the water's glow.

name: Full Throttle
lore: “Few may know this, but the Skull Crusher uses just a fragment of the Pyre's kinetic potential. This is intended for the strain on the train would be too great should the full power of the Pyre be used. In dire circumstances, however, I've included a means to unleash the train's full capabilities.”—Herzal, “My Workshop, My Life”

name: Umbra Stone
lore: As a single mind, the Umbra had no need for written text. But when I finally discovered them, they created a language to converse with me and the other lowly residents of Hell.

name: Deadly Plunge
description: Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to [effect0.power_unmodified]x this friendly unit's [health] and [armor].
lore: “When all seemed lost, Commander Fel descended on our enemies with a divine strike.”—Tome of the Lost Path

name: Engine Upgrade
lore: A substantial upgrade to the furnaces in the Boneshaker will eventually be necessary to ensure more efficient energy output. These upgrades will require considerable room to function, though.

name: Alloy of the Ancients
lore: An alloy of unknown components said to come from the ancient Umbra. Some demons choose to drink it while others just pour it over themselves, letting the alloy create a natural defense.

name: Pyre Shards
lore: To protect the Pyre should it ever feel threatened, I enhanced it to change its shape into something sharper that would damage the attacker. If broken off, these shards can be ingested by the Awoken to achieve the same effect.

name: Pyrecask
lore: A barrel full of Pyregel is perfect, not just for dousing enemies. It is also a wonderful option to bring to a potluck.

name: Spreading Spores
description: Restore [effect2.power] health. Apply [regen] [effect0.status0.power] and [spikes] [effect1.status0.power]. Add a copy of this card to your discard pile.
lore: When thorns find their mark, they release spores into the air to incapacitate unsuspecting victims. These poor souls soon transform into Awoken and feed the vines that first spread the spores. On the embarrassingly frequent occasions that I'm stung by these thorns, I remove them before any real damage occurs.

name: Machinist's Tome
lore: “When the Boneshaker was scattered throughout the Void along with its army, all I had were the scattered scraps, old blueprints, and my father's notebook to aid me in constructing the Skull Crusher. Which is why I hope that, whatever may come from this new enemy we face, this book will aid future generations.—Heph, introduction to “My Workshop, My Life”

name: Slam
description: [advance]. Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to this unit's current [health] and [armor].

name: Risky Operation
description: Reduce friendly unit to [effect0.power] health. Apply +[effect1.power][attack] and [lifesteal] [effect2.status0.power].
lore: “Fascinating! The subject barely survived but look how strong they are!”—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Shelter
lore: Manufactured architecture within the cairns is scarce and any effort that could be used to carve out the walls of the Bogwurm is instead focused on the protection of Echoes and Kinstones. So, Wurmkin choose to dwell — if they rest at all — inside the discarded carapaces of Kinhost. The hard shell is preserved by the Echoes infused within it and ensure that the carapace remains sturdy long after other shells would grow brittle and crumble.

name: Sting
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to the front enemy unit. [halfbreak]Draw +[effect1.power] next turn.
lore: Some trees drop acorns to seed new life - the Awoken shoot thorns. To protect myself, I wore thick leather armor on my first visit to the Wildwood. I can't say it helped much...

name: Runespeak III
description: Draw a damage spell and grant it +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage] [magicpower].

name: Soldier of Fortune
description: Draw a unit. If you have [effect0.secondarypower][coin], spend it to apply +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack], [avarice] [effect0.upgrade.status0.power], and [armor] [effect0.upgrade.status1.power].
lore: “A soldier who goes to war without the promise of pay is a fool with a sword.” —The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #22

name: Secret Ingredient
lore: Not all ingredients in this concoction are rare, fragile, or even illegal. Sometimes all you need is a bit of salt to make a potion all the more potent.

name: Titanstooth
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to enemy units and apply [frostbite] [effect1.status0.power].
lore: Ceremonial spears are given to the Stygian Guard to aid them in their protection of the Unnamed's resting place. Originally just part of tradition, these spears have recently become essential in our defense of Hell.

name: Spider Assembly
description: Add a Spikedriver Spider to your hand, then [craft] it.

name: Power of Knowledge
description: Deal [trait0.power] damage for each consumed spell.
lore: “Echoes are remembered knowledge,” as stoneform dictates. The collective knowledge of the Realm is contained in these crystals and at the disposal of the Wurmkin. They use the Echoes as a sort of library, taking and restoring knowledge at will to solve the work at hand. It is true that knowledge is powerful, but even this much knowledge, on the truth of what happened, is too much for any being to bear. Do not mistake my cowardice for heroism.

name: Cryptcall
description: [raise] [effect0.power] random units and apply an additional +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack].

name: Bramble Lash
description: Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to [trait0.power]x [spikes] on friendly units.
lore: A single, concentrated influx of Wildwood sap can enlarge the thorns of an Awoken for a short time. Through some ill-advised experiments, I've discovered that several simultaneous injections can have devastating effects.

name: Liquid Courage
lore: Sunlight with a sprinkle of courage in a bottle.

name: Echo Vault
description: At the end of the turn, the last spell played on this floor is played again.
lore: “Any good spell is one that repeats itself,” she murmured. The Stone before her hand seemed to drain, no, absorb her magic. The wall trembled, just like a bowstring being pulled back.

name: Inferno Room
description: Deal [effect0.upgrade.roommodifier0.effect0.power] damage to all units at the start of combat.
lore: Let's just say that if you spray Pyregel everywhere, things tend to get a bit... ‘fiery'.

name: Equalizing Rings
description: This unit's [attack] is equal to its max health.
lore: Two gold rings that might have once belonged to a couple who loved each other with a deep, true love. Along the edge, there is a faint inscription and the words ‘for my beloved' can be read.

name: Forevermore Serum
lore: “The serum was meant to get rid of my wrinkles but ended up doing so much more.”—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Steward's Quarters
description: +[effect0.upgrade.roommodifier0.power][capacity]. Shield Steward and Spear Steward units gain [multistrike] [effect0.upgrade.status0.power] and +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack].
lore: Once the train car where Herzal kept his creations, Heph now tinkers deep into the night on her father's Stewards.

name: Inhale
lore: Even the smallest shroomfolk have found ways to defend themselves. Some, when inhaled, consume the lungs of their victims from the inside out.

name: Smith
description: [forge] [effect0.power]. Apply [armor] [effect1.status0.power] to the front friendly unit.
lore: “The Shroud was a beautiful nascent shadow when I began to learn blacksmithing within the Crucible. One day, I stood looking across Limbo towards Heaven and realized that I had not let my hammer from my hand in days. My role as Judge was replaced with that of Blacksmith. And I knew peace.” —Herzal, “My Workshop, My Life”

name: Selfless Sacrifice
lore: “When you have no more weapons in your arsenal, all you can offer is yourself.”—Banished motto

name: Bloodsoaked Arena
lore: The Crimson Arena claimed many disobedient angels, whether by combat or by fall. Those who proved their worth became useful champions, but always held under a tight leash. —Tome of the Lost Path

name: Rage Room
lore: On the rare night when the flames of Hell have dwindled to no more than smoldering embers, the Hellhorned tradition is to rekindle them by using their rage and destroying everything in sight.

name: Razorsharp Edge
lore: Dried out vines can deal more deadly blows, but they risk shattering more easily than their hydrated counterparts. My efforts at strengthening these embrittled appendages have proven fruitless.

name: Hallowed Halls
description: Kill friendly units. [halfbreak]Reform random units to this floor until it exceeds its [size].
lore: Wurmkin stoneform speaks of passageways deep below those controlled by the Wickless, further even than the caverns of the Reformed. These halls of stone sleep in the dark, their floors covered in the wicks of lost Waxers. Should Wax ever fall from the Ring above, and flame come to the wicks that lay there, a soul is said to live again for a brief moment of time. In my darkest nightmares, I rest in these wicked halls forever flickering between life and death.

name: Hoist
description: Move a non-boss unit to this floor.

name: Subsuming Blade
lore: This blade grows larger with each use, slowly accumulating more wax and becoming more dangerous. Reluctantly, I created it with the Wickless when Hell was invaded to defend against the advancing Winged.

name: Tome of Contracts
description: Reduce a unit's [cooldown] Timer by [effect0.powerabs] to a minimum of 1.
lore: “All dragons must sign their name in the ledger and give half their yearly coin to my temple. If they break their contract, refer to the second Rule.”—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #1

name: Bloody Moon
lore: “When Seraph came to destroy our home, the moon shone red. At the sight, Lady Ekka grieved the souls that would fall in the upcoming battle.”—Ardania the Forbidden

name: Meat Shield
lore: A small plate made for the Bone Dog during a birthday ‘paint your own ceramics' party.

name: Surgical Strike
lore: “I‘ve found that the scalpel is mightier than the sword. It can cut with more deadly precision.”—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Sanctuary
lore: “The Outpost would become a sanctuary for all those threatened by Heaven—be they Angel or Demon—and a place of safety from the plague that had consumed the Empyrial Palace.”—Tome of the Lost Path

name: Vampire's Tooth
lore: “The name is a little tongue-in-cheek, my assistant wanted eternal life so I made her an implant that would let her, let's say, ‘drink the life force' of others.”—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Deathroar
description: Transfer all [pyregel] on this floor to a unit then deal [effect1.power] damage five times.
lore: Lady Gilda turned away from the conversation. Her bodyguard, Vagar, was a loyal dragon but his breath was terrible.

name: Imp Toss
description: Kill all [imp] units. Deal [effect0.power] damage per [imp] to enemy units.

name: Cursed Twinblade
lore: “She told me the blades would kill me. I laughed and took the weapon. I was living on borrowed time anyway.”—Finna the Doomed

name: Greed
lore: Leave the gold for the dragons or else they'll add you to their treasure pile.

name: Fertile Ground
description: [spawn] [effect0.power]. [spawn] [trait0.power] more for each card in your consume pile.
lore: “Poor soldier. We'll put him back together,” whispered the fungi beneath the battlefield. “Your body will be a perfect place for us to grow.”

name: Energy Siphon
lore: Lodestones require direct operation to absorb the energy gained from any living beings around them. Through mechanisms I've not been able to understand, the energy retrieved is many times the source's power.

name: Funguy in a Suit
lore: “I'll be the arm!” said one mushroom. “And I'll be the head!” said another. A small voice spoke from the bottom of the armor, “Why do I have do be down here?”

name: Enflame
lore: Deep within the Scorched Plains, Hellhorned Demons can sometimes be seen performing a “magma-walk” - a bizarre coming-of-age ritual involving full submersion into lava and a focused trek across the Plain. It's unbelievable that any Demons survive the ritual, but those that do are stronger for it.

name: Firestarter
lore: An incendiary mixture developed by the Pyreborne to add a little spark to battle.

name: Moon Ritual
lore: “Each new moon phase calls for a new ritual with your fellow fae.”—The Ritual Tome

name: Entropic Crystals
lore: I've seen angels who were once my friends stumble from the weight of Entropy's possession: crystal shards that grow beneath the skin and pierce the body once full control has been established.

name: Transcendimp
description: When played, repeat all [summon] effects triggered so far this battle.

name: Pox
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage and apply [decay] [effect1.status0.power] to all units.
lore: The soldiers moved with uncertain steps towards the Fatal Elm. “Pray to your gods,” came a whisper from beneath the mulch. Spore clouds erupted. “For you are to receive the Mushroom's Kiss.”

name: Alchemy
lore: “A clever dragon can convince all others that they can make air into gold.”—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #53

name: Wildwood Tome
lore: An ancient text of the Channelers of the Edge Priory, this tome outlines its creation. Sadly, the language is closely guarded by the Priory and I've had little luck in translating it.

name: Bloodthirsty Blade
lore: Pulled from the embers of the Pyre, legend tells that one day a leader bearing this sword will lead Hell and Heaven to peace.

name: Geared Gauntlet
lore: Forged of the very gears that propelled the Skull Crusher, each component winds back to deliver attacks at a velocity and rate that challenge that of the train itself. The drawback, however, is a shorter lifespan and unreliable performance. If pushed too far, this gear could permanently damage the driver wheels.

name: Pyreclasm
lore: “And when you have followed my commandments and led a life devoted to gold, then your spirit will experience an explosive transformation.” —The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #1071

name: Pyrespeak
description: Add a 0[ember]Pyreshot to your hand with [consume].

name: Soul Siphon
lore: Over time I've learned that for all of their brushed aside realities, the Wurmkin are more merciful than they let on. The souls they harvest are given a draught to help them rest. To help them forget. It's time I put these memories to bed once more and partake in a similar sort of revelry.

name: Prismal Dust
lore: The dust gathered from mining Prism stones can be collected to create a similar, though less effective, defensive support around the owner.

name: Lunar Echo
description: Create an [ephemeral] copy of a random spell played last turn.

name: Everlasting Light
lore: “I gripped my spear, knowing they would take it away from me. They blamed it for my success in the arena. In the end, I gave it to Talos. May it serve her as well as it did I.”—Finna the Doomed

name: Calcified Ember
lore: Most Ember, a byproduct of the energy within the Pyre, was encased in stone and ice when Hell froze. This made it inaccessible, and unusable, by our train.

name: Enchanted Chamber
lore: Building the train was a true test of engineering. But not all solutions could be hammered away. Sometimes it's useful to know a thing or two about magic.

name: Shroud Spike
description: Trigger feeding on a friendly [snack] unit [trait0.power][x] times.
lore: The Umbra Shroud was the first clan to agree with me that the Rail was crucial to the survival of Hell. This alliance proved my proposed Covenant's importance to the other clans.

name: Packed Morsels
description: Add [effect0.secondarypower] uncommon or rare [snack] units to your hand.
lore: Through an unusual course of events, I've found that bottling many Morsels together allows them to be easily transported to quickly provide labor where it's needed. It also had the added benefit of soothing the little creatures.

name: Inferno
lore: The Scorched Plains are known for frequent firestorms that can rain down at any moment, striking anyone unlucky enough to be caught below. This has made my travels through it particularly short.

name: Awakening Thicket
description: Friendly units have +[effect0.upgrade.unhealedbonushp] max health and restore [effect0.upgrade.charactertrigger0.effect0.power] health on [resolve].
lore: A soul, once put to sleep by spores, is trapped by the vines of the Wildwood only to become Awoken. It's not a very pleasant event to witness, but there is a certain beauty in it all.

name: Ambient Charge
lore: There is a large gap in the Wurmkin's record of their history, an odd occurence for beings so intent on the preservation of knowledge. I've pieced together that during the Wurmkin's rise to power, many Echoes were left unaccounted for, sealed away by the Kinhost in forgotten tunnels. Many that have been found have gone dark, their knowledge lost forever, but occasionally some are found that have fed off the passing souls above. It seems even this latent charge has been enough to preserve them.

name: Last Stand
description: Double the amount of [rage] on friendly units.
lore: It's impossible for the Hellhorned to regain their standing after their horns have been broken, but that doesn't mean they can't fight back against their aggressor to salvage what remains of their reputation.

name: Invigorating Solution
lore: After their first visit aboard my train, the Edge Priory concocted a solution of Wildwood sap and condensed train steam to coax more performance from the Boneshaker's engines.

name: Rootseeds
lore: In one of these dreams, that I'm beginning to believe are visions of the past, Wyldenten showed me the creation of the Wildwood itself: seeds taken from Wyldenten's own body. His final gift before his Exile.

name: Branding Rite
lore: The focused application of heat on a Hellhorned hide will force it to calcify and provide a natural defense. Though I can tell you that the smell is truly...unique.

name: Sharpen
lore: I've found discarded Hollow armor serves as a perfect tool to sharpen dull weapons.

name: Broken Memories
description: Return a consumed spell to the top of your draw pile.
lore: Divines be Damned! Take it back, all of it! I don't want this memory, this power, this grief. I gave it up once and I'll do it again if it means I can live in peace. Have the years of endless labor not been enough to atone? Will it ever be enough!

name: Onehorn's Tome
description: Apply [fragile] and [multistrike] [effect0.status0.power] to a friendly unit.
lore: “Hell's Horns, History of the Hellhorned”, by Grrrg Onehorn. The terrible handwriting of the imp scribes has made this tome an excruciating read and something I don't plan on returning to soon.

name: Dripfall
lore: While Wax Drips are beneficial for those who refuse to melt, getting caught in the downfall can have violent consequences. Consequently, I've decided only to study them from a safe distance.

name: Hidden Passage
lore: Not all routes through the Boneshaker are immediately recognizable. I sealed many of them off to all but those who are willing to tear through steel and squeeze through the shreds.

name: Ancient Resonance
description: Deal [trait0.power] damage to enemy units per [corrupt].
lore: I could not Judge anymore, the simple scale laid out by the Divines too reductive for my beliefs. Souls are complicated, morally ambiguous beings. Hell and Heaven aren't that different, each one having its faults, but also having its wonderful beauties. I am not proud of what I did, nor what came after. The only solace is that, at the time, I believed it to be right, and without that conviction we are all lost. Though, I doubt Seraph will see it the same way.

name: Drain
lore: While the Guard claims that the Titan still sleeps, it seems to show a base level awareness when it is near another soul, helping its kin and hurting everyone else. I've yet to be subjected to either, so I can't say which I am considered.

name: Retch
description: Return eaten units to your hand.
lore: Even the Shroud knows little restraint, sometimes consuming Morsels when, as far as I can tell, no hunger remains. This compulsion, unfortunately, can lead to… ”involuntary expulsion.”

name: Ancient Synergy
description: Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to [trait0.power]x the number of spells in your deck, three times.
lore: When mages channel the energy of the Titan, it is often released uncontrollably and violently at first. It takes many years of studying to control the flow, and while I've studied with the Stygian for a long time, the power still escapes me.

name: Vengeful Shard
lore: When Hell was frozen, the Pyre itself was largely extinguished. The remains that I was unable to collect have been scattered throughout Hell, with Seraph controlling most of them. Some have been corrupted entirely, lashing out at their previous host if they come into too close of contact.

name: Assembly Room
lore: “War pounded at the doors to our forge. The steward manufacturing was too slow, inefficient, and there was no time. My daughter and I combined our expertise—she in the structural, I in the mechanical—and designed a train room that could fabricate new stewards as we needed.”—Herzal, “My Workshop, My Life”

name: Insatiable Hunger
lore: “Some return from the Reanimation Lab with a peculiar hunger that consumes their minds. My assistant Hugo implores that we stop and that our efforts are forbidden.”—from Dr. Orechi's notebooks

name: Feast
description: Trigger feeding on friendly units with [eaten].
lore: Gorgers patrol the mines to collect errant Morsels, consuming them to return them back to the Shroud. They take great pleasure in their purpose, often consuming more Morsels than necessary.

name: Blazing Bolts
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to the front enemy unit. Add a stronger version of this card to your discard.
lore: Constructed bolts I gifted to the Umbra to dig deeper into the stone. When Morsels cannot break through it, these white-hot steel bolts should get the job done.

name: Chomp
description: Destroy a friendly unit and gain +[effect1.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] and +[effect1.upgrade.bonushp][health]. Triggers [gorge] and [eaten].

name: Herzal's Hammer
lore: “It is time to come to terms with who I am. I am a Titan, born to judge souls in Limbo. I cannot change my past, but I can no longer spend my life denying it.”—Herzal, “My Workshop, My Life”

name: Make It Rain
description: Deal [effect1.power] damage to enemy units. Spend [effect2.powerabs][coin] and repeat this card's effect, up to three more times.
lore: Although it goes against the instincts of every dragon in Hell, sometimes you have to loosen the purse strings to win the battle.

name: Crypt Builder
description: [retreat] the front enemy unit and deal [effect0.power] damage.
lore: Massive hammers were used to seal the Titan in its crypt. Requiring the strength of multiple Guards to swing true, these tools have not been moved since their last use.

name: Fracture
lore: The glowing crystals found throughout the tunnels below — Echoes as the Wurmkin call them — hold a dormant power. This power is ancient, to be sure, but strangely familiar. Yet, the more I walk these musty tunnels, the more I begin to feel these Echoes stir.

name: Fight Club
lore: First rule: don't talk about it.

name: Flash Freeze
lore: After the freezing of Hell, the Stygian Sea's weather became much more erratic. Instant freezes are now frequent occurrences, much to the dismay of anyone unlucky enough to be caught in their icy grasp.

name: Superheated
description: Double the amount of [pyregel] on a unit.
lore: “Beneath the Pyreborne's caves flows a river of Pyregel that runs so hot, it erodes the very stone itself. Watch where you step, you might get a superheated surprise.”—Dante's Travel Guide

name: Imp-in-a-Box
description: Add [effect0.secondarypower] random [imp] units to your hand.
lore: Whoever thought to put imps in a confined space had clearly never interacted with the little devils. That didn't stop me from keeping a few boxes. Though, every once in a while, one finally does get out.

name: Curse of Entropy
description: Apply [sap] [effect0.status0.power] to friendly units on all floors.
lore: The Titans, within their nature, each work towards their own twisted form of peace. For Entropy, eternal peace can only be achieved through the stasis of all things.

name: Scrap for Parts
description: Draw a unit and apply +[effect1.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] and 0[ember].
lore: “All these under-performing technicians are still good for something.”—Dr. Orechi

name: Brain Transfer
description: Transfer [attack] and all [buff] and [debuff] effects to front friendly unit.
lore: “While a body can still be usable if preserved correctly, brain matter must be transferred to a host within hours.”—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Small Gift Box
description: Add all [effect0.power] contained spell cards to your hand. [effect0.unboxedcardname]
lore: A gift box with a large card saying: “It isn't the trip, it is the journey. It isn't the gift, it is the container.”-Reese P. Taculum

name: Runespeak II
description: Draw a damage spell and grant it +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage] [magicpower].

name: Ritual Tome
lore: “May all fae, noble and not, write their spells in this tome. For each voice belongs to the coven's chorus.”—The Ritual Tome

name: Echo Bloom
lore: My memory would likely never have been recovered if it were not for the Wurmkin's Echoes. I can finally say that I remember it all now, facing Armageddon, betraying the Divinities, even my attempt to bury the past. Although I could erase a soul's memories, even my own, it seems my powers could not reach these Echoes.

name: Hellfurnace
description: When a unit gains [pyregel], it gains +[effect0.upgrade.roommodifier0.power] stacks.
lore: “We're behind schedule! Pick it up, double-time!” Fenix's voice blared from the forge speaker. The dragonsmiths hammered away, determined to meet their quota.

name: Immortal Trade
description: Apply [lifesteal] [effect0.status0.power] and [emberdrain] [effect1.status0.power] to a friendly unit.
lore: An unfortunate outcome of our invention, Void consumption has become an addictive practice amongst the Umbra. When that no longer satiates their hunger, the entire replacement of self with these Void shards becomes the only way to gain any satisfaction.

name: Resin Removal
description: Remove all [debuff] effects from friendly units and all [buff] effects from enemy units.
lore: When wax hardens into resin, it is possible to chip away the crystallized exterior to expose the soft wax underneath. The process does not come without risks, though.

name: Torch
lore: The Hellhorned have learned to live with the unpredictability of the Scorched Plains, even going so far as to retain some of the flaming boulders for themselves, despite my attempts to dissuade them.

name: Empower
description: Gain [attack] equal to [pyregel] stacks on all units.

name: Spike of the Stygian
lore: The Stygian Guard was formed with our Rail of the Covenant, created by Tethys to protect the sealed Unnamed Titan. The Guard was wary of our Covenant from the beginning, worried that it would make the Pyre vulnerable to outside attacks. Unfortunately, they were correct.

name: Minds Of Their Own
lore: A scraping sound, like a dead fish being dragged across a plank, caused Hugo to turn. He froze. The hand he had just collected was gone!

name: Electricity Chamber
lore: “When an assistant has fallen, take them to the chamber so that their bodies can be reawakened with a little zap.”—OHELL Safety Regulations and Guidelines

name: Fortified Pauldrons
lore: Leather is a common material among the Hellhorned, so I've lined my garb with the material for protection. Given the stench, I'm sure the source of it is better left a mystery.

name: Primitive Mold
lore: Fade brought me to the site of a rock split in two. The shape reminded me of the molds used by the Melting Remnant, and the drips of wax made this theory more plausible. Fade says she split the rock because she was bored, but her subsequent silence seems to suggest a more altruistic purpose. Why are they showing me these things?

name: Void Armament
lore: When Void shards were first found, they were considered to be of little value. No one expected that they could be pulled together in a weapon that doubled any attack's force.

name: Glass Cannon
lore: As powerful as this weapon is, it is just as fragile. Handle with care.

name: Organ Harvester
lore: “My experiments tend to take a toll on my the bodies of my assistants. I made this contraption so I could collect new parts with more efficiency.”—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Focused Growth
lore: I've observed from those of the Wildwood that with great concentration comes great healing. The Awoken can channel their will into sprouting spores on the surface of their form to heal broken parts of their vined bodies.

name: Boom
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to the front enemy.

name: Rot
lore: When he drew his hand back from the tree's roots, he found spores had settled on his skin like dust. First, he felt warm, then hot. Until his limb was engulfed in the unbearable pain of rotting alive.

name: Returned Soul
description: Return a spell from the discard pile to your hand. Apply [infused] and [consume].
lore: Learning this strange language on the stones was slowgoing at first, but as if by some stroke of divinity, I'm now able to decipher the runes quickly. I wouldn't go so far as to say I'm fluent, but this odd influx of knowledge has been remarkable and likely the result of the Wurmkin's Echoes injecting me with it on their own will. Will they take it away just as easily?

name: Dante's Inferno
description: Deal damage to enemy units on all floors equal to [trait1.power]x the number of Dante's Candle cards in your deck.
lore: Little is known of Dante, but what I've seen of his magic puts fear in my heart. I am just glad that he is on our side, for now.

name: Echo Break
lore: I, along with all of Hell, had assumed the Bogwurm's Remains to hold nothing but death and decay. The Rail had been built without the Ring's consent, the life found above ground appearing to show no sentience. So, when I found a clan, a civilization even, that existed within the excavated remains of the Bogwurm, I realized that there are more holes to my knowledge than I previously assumed.

name: Cryptcall II
description: [raise] [effect0.power] random units and apply an additional +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack].

name: Forced Contamination
lore: The Echoes' hunger for souls is what ultimately led to my discovery of this place. Their appetite had grown beyond the souls that were lured below so the Echoes had begun to extend their powers to the surface, leeching souls directly from those that would choose to wander the Bogs.

name: Scissor Hands
lore: “Well, at least making confetti will be easy.”

name: Metallurgy
description: [smelt] a card in hand. Apply [armor] [effect0.status0.power] to friendly units.
lore: “A machine is only as trustworthy as the metal beneath its paint. Every new alloy must be tested to withstand the Pyre itself before it is put to work.”—Herzal, “My Workshop, My Life”

name: Grovel
description: Apply [damageshield] [effect0.status0.power]. Add [effect1.secondarypower] uncommon or rare [snack] units to your hand.
lore: Some errant Morsels, in an effort to please the Wardens, will offer their valuable jewels to try and get in their good graces. This behavior has been noted for future bribes that occur within the Boneshaker.

name: Cosmic Bolt
lore: A flash was all the warning Seraph got.

name: Channelsong
description: Draw a unit and apply +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack], +[effect0.upgrade.bonushp][health], and 0[ember].
lore: The Channelers of the Wildwood prefer to keep their involvement in its growth to a minimum. However, their intervention is sometimes required to achieve more “aggressive” expansion.

name: Shadesplitter
description: Add a common or uncommon [snack] unit to your hand.
lore: While the Umbra Shroud cannot do any physical labor on its own, it can create Antumbra Morsels to follow simple instructions and extract the full value of the Crucible. The splitting of the Shroud is like nothing I've ever seen before, and, frankly, prefer not to see again.

name: Pandemic
description: Apply [decay] [effect1.status0.power] and [sap] [effect2.status0.power]. Add a copy of this card to your discard pile.
lore: “I know she's our enemy but I just can't help myself, I'm in love!” said the angel. “You too?! I feel as if I've been infected with love!” hissed his captain.

name: Dante's Candle
lore: I've seen Dante roam beyond the walls of the Outpost, collecting souls to store and burn when he most needs them.

name: Mix-a-Lot
lore: “By the time I realized what her experiments were doing to her, it was too late. Inga's sanity was as small and weak as a flicker of light in an endless night.”—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Tome of the Lost Path
description: Apply [ability]: Flight to a friendly unit.
lore: “If one day I fall, I hope that this record will remind future fighters of the sacrifices Finna made to save them.”—Tome of the Lost Path

name: Iron-tongue
description: This unit's [attack] is set to [effect0.upgrade.status0.power] and cannot be changed.
lore: “I used to think my father was naive for believing peace was possible. Until one day I stumbled upon a weapon in the dunes of Limbo that had both angelic and demonic markings.”—Tales of the Inferno

name: Echo Transfer
lore: I cannot yet decipher all of their symbols etched into the stone, but the Wurmkin's stoneforms describe the creation of these Echoes as part of a great Titan sacrifice. The Titan's knowledge lives on in the perfect crystalline structures. More sacrifice and exile, but for what?

name: Flicker
lore: “A small flicker can still burn.”—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #37

name: Tome of Evergrowth
description: Apply [ability]: Evergrowth to a friendly unit.
lore: The archive of the Wild Woods and the Hell Oak from which Underlegion are spawned.

name: Magnetic Relay
description: Return a non-champion friendly unit and its attached equipment to your hand.
lore: Magnets originally built to gather and sort metal for the junkyard were often used aboard the train, to recover errant stewards who, for one reason or another, found their way overboard. A malfunctioning steward is rare, though such incidents raise questions on if such stewards were acting on their own accord, rather than that of their creator.

name: Icestorm
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to a random enemy unit, five times.
lore: When Hell was frozen, the Stygian Sea was cursed with an eternal storm, making my travel across it near impossible. Fortunately, I was later saved by the Guard, but the invaders of Hell were not so lucky.

name: Memorial for the Melted
lore: The Reformed, a group of Waxers dedicated to the melting of others, believe in respecting the already melted. The Reformed keep the wicks of each Waxer they've helped to melt, burning the wicks briefly to remind themselves of their own impermanence, but extinguishing the wicks quickly to remember that their purpose is not yet fulfilled.

name: Forgotten Trade
lore: Today I found it — my life, given up. It's comforting, I suppose, to know that my mind isn't truly lost, but the truth I've found, of mistakes and guilt, are a consolation not suited for the offense. Exiles sacrificed at my behest. Judgement forsaken to save human souls. Titans destroyed by my hand. All ending in the loss of our Realm. As a Titan, a Judge even, I was supposed to make no error, yet I doomed the very ground upon which I walk. What do I know of judgement...

name: Inequivalent Exchange
description: Deal damage equal to [trait0.power]x your [dragonshoardicon], then lose [effect1.powerabs][dragonshoardicon].
lore: “Here's your change,” said a voice. These words were the angel's only warning before a barrage of coins flew straight towards him.

name: Accelerated Incubation
lore: Stoneform dictates strict control of Wurmkin population. I've seen thousands of eggs hibernating throughout the tunnels, but never realized that the Wurmkin directly control the time of their hatching. The Rail was my solution to this immortal overpopulation, so it's exciting to see another.

name: Boilerplate
lore: “The only steel I trust is the kind that doesn't buckle under the Pyre's pressure. If a boiler can endure that heat, a breastplate can endure anything else.”—Herzal, “My Workshop, My Life”

name: Crystalline Seeds
lore: I've been able to capture shards of ice from the now-frozen sea and distill them into seed crystals, making the instantaneous freezing of objects even easier.

name: Unleash the Wildwood
description: Restore friendly units to full health.
lore: The vines of the Wildwood stockpile harvested energy to use during unexpected droughts. When these stores are tapped into, the energy provides a surge of new life and power to the host.

name: Deadly Variant
lore: The angel tried to escape the frenzy of battle but it was too late. The Fatal Elm had its spores in him. Soon, they would eat away at him and transform his body until he was more fungus than flesh.

name: Scrap Metal
lore: Torn parts from the Skull Crusher, broken Stewards, fragmented blades from both enemy and allies, all these must be kept and stored for future need. Especially now as the Skull Crusher hurdles towards an unknown enemy and few know what awaits.

name: Pyreshot
description: The Pyre immediately attacks enemy units on this floor.
lore: “The memories of my time as Judge pain me but I must force myself to remember for the sake of the Pyre. Something calls out to it from beyond Limbo. A mother's voice perturbs the sands between Heaven and Hell and sends altered souls against us. Like a Child longing for its Mother, the Pyre struggles to break free. And, sometimes, it is successful.”—Herzal, “My Workshop, My Life”

name: Ritual of Battle
lore: I have learned that the Hellhorned can gain temporary strength through the self-infliction of pain. I find the ritual savage, but it proves to be even more effective when performed over the remains of their opponents.

name: Heavensward
description: [ascend] friendly units, then [advance] the highest [health] friendly unit on the new floor.
lore: “And as we follow the Rail into battle to reclaim Heaven from the Titans, the spirit of the fallen will be carried by those who yearn for freedom. For we that have been tried in the furnace of expulsion will form a single, tremendous force that will bring peace to all!”—final chapter of the Tome of the Lost Path

name: Glimmer
description: Restore [effect0.power] health to friendly units and deal [effect1.power] damage to enemy units.
lore: If struck by a surge of electricity, a Sapwood will crystallize into glass. The sap within will become preserved as a supercharged healing solvent. But I can't seem to break the glass without losing much of this sap in the process.

name: Eagleheart
description: [advance]. Apply [valor] [effect1.status0.power] to a friendly unit, then it attacks immediately.
lore: “And as she was lifted in the air, Fel felt the will of her soldiers give her strength.” —Tome of the Lost Path

name: Ensnare
lore: The Wildwood of Hell encases those that linger too long underneath its draping canopy. These living trees scare me more than I care to admit.

name: Resurgence III
description: Remove [stasis] and gain +[effect1.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] and +[effect1.upgrade.bonushp][health] per [stygianblessing]. Removes ability on use.

name: Stardust Invocation
description: [phase]. Create an [ephemeral] copy of a spell in your hand.
lore: “Take a handful of stardust and whisper an incantation over it. Your spell's power will be doubled.”—The Ritual Tome

name: Enfeebling Infusion
lore: “It took a lot of kitten whiskers but I finally made a drink that cripples a subject. Now, what will I do with all these adorable felines?”—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Explosive Reaction
lore: “My contraption taps into the celestial core of angels and makes them... well, let's just say they put on a good light show.”—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Loamcoat
lore: The dapperling special ops unit knows the importance of good soil to a shroom's performance. They went one step further and found a way to bring soil to the battlefield.

name: Cannibalize
description: Add [effect1.power] uncommon or rare [snack] units to your hand.
lore: Despite being a hive-minded creature, the Umbra Shroud still falls victim to the petty squabbles observed in the other clans. It's unclear how this hive-minded creature can argue with itself, but the ensuing scuffles can be deadly and something I've learned to detect and avoid.

name: Waxen Spike
lore: The alliance of the Rings of Hell also created an alliance between the Reformed and the Wickless Remains, bringing together the separate groups under Flicker. To seal their pact, they created a Railspike from their collective wax and drove it into our Rail.

name: Salvage
lore: “War does not forgive waste. A broken sword can be renewed. A dented Steward must be fixed. Maybe one day we will have space for excess but, for now, every bit of steel is essential.”—Herzal, “My Workshop, My Life”

name: Double-Edged Arms
lore: Inspired by the Hell Lobster's own appendages, these pincers can grip, cut, and twist the most stubborn of materials.

name: Scrap Harvest
description: Add a Scrap Metal to your hand.

name: Imp-pressive
description: Deal [effect1.power] damage to the front enemy unit.
lore: “Some Imps eat Pyre. While Pyre tasty, Pyre not endless. Hungry imps then eaten by Pyre. And life continues.” -excerpt from Hell's Horns by Grrrg Onehorn on Pyre-eating etiquette.

name: Spell Sanctum
lore: “Carved these runes myself. A bit of magic here, and some engineerin' there.”—Heph

name: Eternal Kinstone
lore: Once the Wurmkin have completed their kinstone, they commit that knowledge to a cairn. “Truth, Forever” as they put it. Do you think they account for the truths that rip you open inside? No, they put a stone in a crypt for all to see and to know. For all eternity, damn the consequences. Some things are best left forgotten.

name: Blast Infusion
lore: “I did not anticipate that my concoction would be so explosive, but I am happy with the result. Best to keep it a secret. My assistants would not understand.”—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Beacon's Light
description: Apply [dazed] [effect0.status0.power] to enemy units on all floors.
lore: The Beacon's light swallows up every shape and shadow. Those foolish enough to meet its gaze will leave with their senses seared away.

name: Fire Breathing
description: Deal damage equal to this unit's attack to enemy units, twice.

name: Divinity
lore: Fel bathed her warriors with an unfamiliar light. Heaven's Light, usually harsh and blinding, became soft. Her warriors sensed it, perhaps Heaven's Light had found a new steward.

name: Wurmkin Spike
lore: The creation of the Wurmkin Spike was an appreciated gesture, but symbolic nonetheless. The Wurmkin never opted into the Rail and had made it clear that they would continue to preserve their anonymity. When I leave — when I forget — the Spike will remain with them, their symbolic support returned along with the memory of my mistakes.

name: Savage Shackles
lore: To my knowledge, the effects of Savagery are more on the mind than on the body. A bloodlust consumes once peaceful angels and turns them into murderous monsters.

name: Oldgrowth
lore: Where the Hollow leave behind their husks, there are vines that refuse to die. They grow and grow, forestalling their inevitable decay. The Channelers say this is because “She” still lives. Few know what they could mean and even fewer find comfort in their words.

name: Excavated Ember
lore: Even the pressures of time can reverse the effects of calcified Ember. It only takes a worthy soul to carry the load, but one much worthier than myself.

name: Boiler Room
lore: Herzal's original design was for the trains to be fueled only by the Pyre. Heph's updated design allows the train to be fueled by traditional methods as well, making the system more efficient overall.

name: Runespeak
description: Draw a damage spell and grant it +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage] [magicpower].

name: Hoarfrost Effigy
description: Transfer all [frostbite] on this floor to a unit, then double the amount of [frostbite].
lore: Even before the freeze, the granite monuments of the Titan dotting the sea were cold structures. Now they've become permanently frozen fixtures of the seascape, ominous presences easily recognizable by their sharp profiles.

name: Mitosis Cap
lore: Death is an opportunity to make a new, better version of yourself. This is a lesson many have known for as long as the roots of the Fatal Elm are deep.

name: Intent on Death
description: Trigger a unit's [extinguish] ability without killing it.
lore: Votive Houses can become crowded and melting away is a long process. To avoid the wait, I've seen some Waxers increase the intensity of their flame through extreme focus, though they typically lose consciousness briefly after doing it.

name: Antumbra Assault
lore: As the first line of defense in the Crucible, Morsels will rocket towards an intruder, often sacrificing themselves in the process. If they succeed in their defense, they live to mine another day.

name: Heavenfall
lore: “If I must fall, may I at least grant you time to escape.”—last words of Ardania, forbidden younger sister of Arduhn and Ekka

name: Hall of Mirrors
description: [effect0.upgrade.roommodifier1.power][capacity]. When you play a unit, create a copy of it.
lore: “This one took a bit of creative engineering. Anything you put in here, you get another one back. Neat trick, eh?”—Heph

name: Vine Grasp
lore: Vined Awoken have been known to lash out to control their enemies. While not an enemy, I too have been lashed and it is a less than pleasant experience.

name: Mushroom Cloud
description: [sacrifice] [effect0.status0.power] [funguy]. Deal [effect2.power] damage and apply [decay] [effect1.status0.power] to enemy units.
lore: “PORCINI GO BOOM!”

name: Spike of the League
lore: Once, Dr. Orechi was someone who would bristle at the thought of his creations being used for war. He sighed and drove his spike into the Rail. Times had changed.

name: Fae's Blessing
description: Restore [effect0.power] health. Healing over max health applies [armor] instead.
lore: Arduhn stretched out his hand towards the fae, who touched him in return. And so a pact was made. The fae would assist the coven so they could return home.

name: Scrap
lore: The Rail is littered with debris that clutter the tracks and will derail your train if you are not careful.

name: Wracking Pain
description: Deal damage equal to [trait0.power]x the [debuff] stacks on this unit.
lore: “The pain... What an amazing olfactory note for my latest scent.”—Madame Lionsmane

name: Lunacy
lore: “Some believe that the Selene control the moon and her phases. What lunacy. The moon can not be forced to do what she does not wish. Time, on the other hand, can be manipulated.”—The Ritual Tome

name: Imp Toss II
description: Kill all [imp] units. Deal [effect0.power] damage per [imp] to enemy units.

name: Chamber of Recall
description: At the end of the turn, return a random consumed spell to your hand.
lore: The Wurmkin claim they contain the History of the World in their stoneform — the knowledge of demons and Titans alike that can be granted and returned at will. I thought my notes to be a near-total collection of information on this Realm, but the Wurmkin appear to know of things that they have no right knowing. Things that, once long ago, I may have known myself...

name: Unearthed Remains
lore: The Wurmkin treat the tunnels of the Bogwurm's Remains as sacred ground, making minor adjustments to the structure to avoid risking its structural stability. Space is limited with no expansions made intentionally. So, when a tunnel collapse leads to a forgotten cavern, you can imagine the Wurmkin's joy — or what passes for joy — at the new space and Echoes to explore.

name: Spell Slam
description: Restore to full health. Apply [spellweakness] [effect1.status0.power] to enemy units.

name: Potion Kit
lore: “An essential collection of tools that every lab technician needs: powdered Titan bone, a beaker, a faulty burner, and chili, of course.”—OHELL Safety Regulations and Guidelines

name: Mixology
lore: “I must admit, I do find myself sometimes getting a little whimsical with my concoctions. Just look at my Hair-Lifting Blueberry Fizzes!”—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Gellysneeze
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage then apply [pyregel] [effect1.status0.power] to the front enemy unit.

name: Mulch
description: Draw +[effect0.power] next turn. For every [trait1.tertiarypower] cards in your deck, draw +[trait1.power] more.
lore: We grow in the shadow of Death.—old Underlegion saying

name: Goliath Infusion
lore: “This is the one. This will make Inga better. But first, I must test it on myself…”—Baron Grael

name: Inspire
lore: To the surprise of all, it was Talos who stood before her fellow soldiers and urged them to continue fighting. “For our homes, for our lives, and for a united future!” she cried.

name: Hallowed Drippings
lore: Those of the Melting Remnant who want to continue living must attend a Votive House to receive a Blessing of Wax. But on some rare occasions, the Reformed will grant a soul some of the sacred wax for use outside the House.

name: Wicked Blaze
lore: Though not entirely under their control, the burning of a Waxer's wick can accelerate with a great deal of focus and help from other Waxers. The resulting melting wax is then collected and donated to reform one of their kin.

name: Remnant Pact
description: Apply [endless] to a friendly unit for the rest of battle.
lore: Despite their age-long feud, the Wickless and the Reformed were able to come to an armistice when the Covenant was formed. That doesn't mean that the rules put in place for their peace were easy to follow.

name: Masterwork
lore: “I once believed the Covenant to be my masterwork, a peace forged between Heaven and Hell. Now, I understand that my greatest work was never something so grand, but was instead, someone. For Heph, my dear daughter, I dedicate this hammer to you.”—Herzal, “My Workshop, My Life”

name: Steel Enhancer
lore: I've used Wildwood sap as a mild steel polish as well, providing combat benefits to the Awoken that receive my treatment.

name: Soulcrushing Guilt
lore: Four Titans for Four Elements: that was the rule created by the Divinities before. Their sacrifice led to our Pyre, our survival. The only knowledge of this has been kept locked in these Wurmkin tunnels. Those that learn of our mistakes are broken with guilt, unable to process the magnitude of what once was. The Wurmkin have removed themselves from blame, seeing their roles as custodians of knowledge penance enough for the original sins.

name: Spike of the Hellhorned
lore: In an act of unity unheard of in Hellhorned culture, Grrrg the Railbeater snapped his own horn to seal the Rail in their Ring, bringing the Hellhorned into our Covenant. Grrrg the Railbeater was thereafter known as Grrrg Onehorn.

name: Swiftsteel Dagger
lore: Angels and Hellborne used all kinds of armaments, but only the Angels made them to be this sleek.

name: Assemble
description: Create a copy of the front friendly non-champion unit and [descend] it.

name: Renovate
lore: “To go up against the Soulstream, the Skull Crusher is goin' to need a few modifications. New cars, stronger steel plates, and better wheels, they all need an upgrade if we're goin' to stand a chance. Take a look. I've got a few blueprints of my ideas…”—Heph

name: It's Alive!
lore: “When I awoke, I did not remember anything of my previous life. It was as if I had been born anew! And this time, I had a few extra special ‘upgrades,' if you will.”—Hugo, assistant to Dr. Orechi

name: Fenix Fire III
description: Deal damage equal to [effect0.power][x] this unit's attack. Apply [pyregel] [effect1.status0.power] to enemy units.

name: Sacrificial Chamber
lore: “If a dragon cannot pay their yearly tribute, they will pay their tithe with their life.”—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #2

name: Awoken's Rail Spike
description: Draw [x] and apply <nobr>-[effect0.upgrade.costreduction][ember]</nobr> to those cards. [halfbreak]Cannot draw additional cards this turn.
